analysis:
The PR contains only documentation: a changelog entry (changelog.d/mixed-step-prefill-chunk.md, lines 1-8) and a new section in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 523-539). No executable code is in the supplied units, so I examined the described behavior only. The prefill geometry change (2,048-token chunks and a 4,096-token step for GPT-OSS, dense Qwen and Gemma 4) sits in code outside this batch (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift), and I could not verify it.

Security-relevant points:
1. Memory and availability (TB-007, T-029). The docs state that a mixed step can now carry up to 4,096 prompt tokens and that this rides the unchanged activation reserve. They also say the measured peak is 0.1 GiB above the GPT-OSS floor and 0.3 GiB above the previous Qwen3.5-9B peak, and that those floors need long-context re-measurement coordinated with platform admission. This is a self-disclosed accuracy and DoS-headroom risk, not a verified regression. A provider that is slightly under-reserved could hit memory pressure under eight concurrent 32k prompts. The code that enforces the cap is not supplied, so I cannot confirm whether the process-wide ledger and cap still bound this.
2. Prefix cache (T-041). The changelog says dense Qwen recurrent prefix checkpoints now land at 2,048-token boundaries rather than 512-token boundaries when prefilled beside decode. This coarsens restore granularity. The TTFT-oracle channel (SEC-035) stays the same in kind, but hit/miss behavior at coarser boundaries may shift slightly. The HMAC lookup tags, TTL, crypto and salt scoping are not changed in the supplied text. The next pass should confirm that checkpoint boundary changes do not alter the SSDPrefixCache donation gate (adoption bound plus the 1,024-token benefit floor).
3. Configuration. The documented DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS overrides disqualify reviewed serving profiles. The forwarding in `darkbloom start` is outside the supplied evidence.

No trust-boundary, authorization, attestation, encryption or data-exposure change is visible. needs_deeper_review is set because the underlying Swift change is not in this batch.
